claims.text: CrCoNi is a single-phase FCC medium-entropy alloy.
CrCoNi has a very low or negative stacking-fault energy relevant to its twinning propensity.
The cited negative stacking-fault energy for CrCoNi was calculated at 0 K.
A hierarchical three-dimensional twin network can form in CrCoNi grains approximately 5–50 μm in size.
Low stacking-fault energy promotes formation of the three-dimensional twin network.
Twin boundaries in the network impede dislocation motion and thereby contribute to strength and strain hardening.
The twin network and its interfaces provide multiple pathways for dislocation motion and slip, permitting substantial plastic deformation.
The twin network delays localized plastic instability and crack initiation.
Twinning-controlled deformation contributes to the combination of high strength, ductility, continuous strain hardening, and exceptional fracture toughness in CrCoNi.
The three-dimensional twin network governs plastic strain and toughness during deformation at 600–800 °C.
CrCoNi-based low-SFE FCC alloys are suited for fusion plasma-facing components.
Adding a small amount of an SFE-raising alloying element will suppress deformation-twin nucleation.
Suppressing twin formation through the compositional adjustment will reduce strain hardening, plastic strain tolerance, and fracture toughness.
At 600–800 °C, the unmodified low-SFE alloy will have significantly higher strain hardening, plasticity, and toughness than the higher-SFE modified alloy.
The proposed mechanism should apply only where twinning remains an active deformation mechanism in a sufficiently low-SFE FCC microstructure.
The mechanism may cease to govern behavior when precipitation hardening, phase transformations, extreme temperature, or irradiation dominates or destabilizes twins.
The twin network is stable against detwinning as deformation continues, with twin-boundary interfaces serving as slip pathways.
The quantitative strengthening contribution of deformation twinning and the resulting property changes are uncertain and system-dependent.
The effectiveness and stability of the twin network under simultaneous high temperature and fusion-relevant irradiation are not established.
